target_text: Strong passwords are long, unique, and boring to anyone but you; reuse is the enemy of security. Everyone expected the team to lose, which is probably why the final goal felt so extraordinary. A good cup of coffee, in my experience, is hot, strong, and shared with someone who knows when to stay quiet. The new bridge, which cost millions of pounds, was closed for repairs within a fortnight of opening. Experts recommend that you back up your files regularly, store a copy elsewhere, and test the restore process. With a sigh, she closed the laptop, stretched her arms above her head, and looked out at the sleepy street. She practised the violin for two hours every evening, even when her fingers ached and the neighbours complained. Zebras, giraffes, and elephants gathered at the waterhole as the sun dipped below the horizon. I can't promise it will be easy, but I can promise that it will be worth every difficult step.

audio.processing: none applied by this app (no gain, filtering, noise reduction or normalisation); float32 -> int16 conversion only

capture.track_label: Microphone Array (Intel® Smart Sound Technology for Digital Microphones)
capture.sample_rate_note: AudioContext created at the microphone's reported rate.
capture.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/156.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

sync.method: performance.now() <-> AudioContext clock pairs sampled every 250 ms, converted to sample indices via the AudioWorklet's frame counter (ctx_frame_of_sample_0), then a least-squares line sample = slope*performance_ms + intercept.

csv_columns.time_ms: performance.now() read at the start of the keydown/keyup handler
csv_columns.event_time_ms: event.timeStamp (browser's own event time, same clock as performance.now())
csv_columns.t_rel_ms: time_ms minus the estimated performance.now() instant of audio sample 0
csv_columns.sample_index_est: estimated audio sample index (round(slope*time_ms+intercept)); NOT sample-accurate

limitations: Synchronisation is estimated, not sample-accurate. Treat sample_index_est as accurate to roughly tens of milliseconds at best.

Microphone, driver, OS and browser input buffering delay the audio relative to the keyboard event. The browser does not expose this input latency, so it is NOT corrected for: sounds appear in the WAV later than sample_index_est suggests by an unknown, roughly constant offset.

getOutputTimestamp() describes the output clock and may differ from the input clock by the output latency; the current_time and worklet_arrival fits are provided for comparison (see model_offset_vs_primary_ms).
Keyboard events are timestamped when the browser dispatches them, which can lag the physical press by a few milliseconds.
Recommended: estimate the residual offset in analysis, e.g. by cross-correlating keydown times with detected click onsets, and apply it to the raw time_ms values.
